title.zh: 卷十二 補列傳第四 文宣四王 孝昭六王 武成十二王 後主五男
title.en: Volume 12 Biographies 4: Four Princes of Wenxuan; Six Princes of Xiaozhao; Twelve Princes of Wucheng; Five Princes of Houzhu
title.raw: 卷十二 補列傳第四 文宣四王 孝昭六王 武成十二王 後主五男 Volume 12 Biographies 4: Four Princes of Wenxuan; Six Princes of Xiaozhao; Twelve Princes of Wucheng; Five Princes of Houzhu

sentences.zh: 文宣四王

translations.literal: The Four Princes of Wenxuan
translations.idiomatic: The Four Princes of Wenxuan

sentences.zh: 太原王紹德 范陽王紹義 西河王紹仁 隴西王紹廉

translations.literal: Prince of Taiyuan Shaode; Prince of Fanyang Shaoyi; Prince of Xihe Shaoren; Prince of Longxi Shaolian
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Taiyuan (Shaode); Prince of Fanyang (Shaoyi); Prince of Xihe (Shaoren); Prince of Longxi (Shaolian)

sentences.zh: 文宣五男：李后生廢帝及太原王紹德，馮世婦生范陽王紹義，裴嬪生西河王紹仁，顏嬪生隴西王紹廉。

translations.literal: Wenxuan had five sons: Empress Li bore the Deposed Emperor and Prince Shaode of Taiyuan; Lady Feng bore Prince Shaoyi of Fanyang; Lady Pei bore Prince Shaoren of Xihe; Lady Yan bore Prince Shaolian of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang had five sons: Empress Li bore the Deposed Emperor and Prince Shaode of Taiyuan; Lady Feng bore Prince Shaoyi of Fanyang; Lady Pei bore Prince Shaoren of Xihe; Lady Yan bore Prince Shaolian of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 太原王紹德，文宣第二子也。

translations.literal: Prince Shaode of Taiyuan was Wenxuan's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shaode of Taiyuan was Gao Yang's second son.

sentences.zh: 天保末，為開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era, he was made Opener of the Way with Honors Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era, he was made opener of the way with honors equal to the three ducal ministers.

sentences.zh: 武成因怒李后，罵紹德曰：「你父打我時，竟不來救！

translations.literal: Because Wucheng was enraged at Empress Li, he cursed at Shaode, saying, "When your father was beating me, you didn't come to save me!
translations.idiomatic: Because Gao Zhan was enraged at Empress Li, he cursed at Shaode, saying, "When your father was beating me, you didn't come to save me!

sentences.zh: 」以刀環築殺之，親以土埋之遊豫園。

translations.literal: " He killed him by striking with the ring of his knife, and personally buried him with earth in the Pleasure Garden.
translations.idiomatic: " He killed him by striking with the ring of his knife, and personally buried him with earth in the Pleasure Garden.

sentences.zh: 武平元年，詔以范陽王子辨才為後，襲太原王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wuping, an edict made Biancai, son of the Prince of Fanyang, his successor to inherit the title Prince of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wuping, an edict made Biancai, son of the Prince of Fanyang, his successor to inherit the title Prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 范陽王紹義，文宣第三子也。

translations.literal: Prince Shaoyi of Fanyang was Wenxuan's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shaoyi of Fanyang was Gao Yang's third son.

sentences.zh: 初封廣陽，後封范陽。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed at Guangyang, later enfeoffed at Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was enfeoffed at Guangyang, later enfeoffed at Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 歷位侍中、清都尹。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Palace Attendant and Governor of Qingdu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to palace attendant and governor of Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 好與羣小同飲，擅置內參，打殺博士任方榮。

translations.literal: He liked to drink with low companions, arbitrarily appointed palace attendants, and beat to death the Erudite Ren Fangrong.
translations.idiomatic: He liked to drink with low companions, arbitrarily appointed palace attendants, and beat to death the erudite Ren Fangrong.

sentences.zh: 武成嘗杖之二百，送付昭信后，后又杖一百。

translations.literal: Wucheng once caned him two hundred strokes and sent him to Empress Zhaoxin; the empress caned him another hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhan once caned him two hundred strokes and sent him to Empress Zhaoxin; the empress caned him another hundred.

sentences.zh: 及後主奔鄴，以紹義為尚書令、定州刺史。

translations.literal: When Houzhu fled to Ye, Shaoyi was made Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor fled to Ye, Shaoyi was made chief minister of the secretariat and governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 周武帝克幷州，以封輔相為北朔州總管。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou captured Bing Province, he made Feng Fuxiang Military Governor of Beishuo Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou captured Bing Province, he made Feng Fuxiang military governor of Beishuo Province.

sentences.zh: 此地齊以重鎮，諸勇士多聚焉。

translations.literal: Qi regarded this place as a strategic stronghold; many brave warriors gathered there.
translations.idiomatic: Qi regarded this place as a strategic stronghold; many brave warriors gathered there.

sentences.zh: 前長史趙穆、司馬王當萬等謀執輔相，迎任城王於瀛州。

translations.literal: The former Administrator Zhao Mu, the Commander Wang Dangwan, and others plotted to seize Fuxiang and welcome the Prince of Rencheng at Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: The former administrator Zhao Mu, the commander Wang Dangwan, and others plotted to seize Fuxiang and welcome the Prince of Rencheng at Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 事不果，便迎紹義。

translations.literal: The affair did not succeed, so they welcomed Shaoyi instead.
translations.idiomatic: The affair did not succeed, so they welcomed Shaoyi instead.

sentences.zh: 紹義至馬邑。

translations.literal: Shaoyi reached Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi reached Mayi.

sentences.zh: 輔相及其屬韓阿各奴等數十人皆齊叛臣，自肆州以北城戍二百八十餘盡從輔相，及紹義至，皆反焉。

translations.literal: Fuxiang and his subordinates Han A'onu and several dozen others were all Qi defectors; from Si Province northward, more than two hundred and eighty garrisons all followed Fuxiang, and when Shaoyi arrived, they all turned.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxiang and his subordinates Han A'onu and several dozen others were all Qi defectors; from Si Province northward, more than two hundred and eighty garrisons all followed Fuxiang, and when Shaoyi arrived, they all turned.

sentences.zh: 紹義與靈州刺史袁洪猛引兵南出，欲取幷州，至新興而肆州已為周守。

translations.literal: Shaoyi and Governor of Ling Province Yuan Hongmeng led troops south, intending to take Bing Province; when they reached Xinxing, Si Province was already held by Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi and Governor of Ling Province Yuan Hongmeng led troops south, intending to take Bing Province; when they reached Xinxing, Si Province was already held by Zhou.

sentences.zh: 前隊二儀同以所部降周。

translations.literal: The vanguard's two Military Companions of the Fourth Rank surrendered to Zhou with their commands.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard's two military companions of the fourth rank surrendered to Zhou with their commands.

sentences.zh: 周兵擊顯州，執刺史陸瓊，又攻陷諸城。

translations.literal: Zhou forces attacked Xian Province, captured the governor Lu Qiong, and also captured several cities.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou forces attacked Xian Province, captured Governor Lu Qiong, and also captured several cities.

sentences.zh: 紹義還保北朔。

translations.literal: Shaoyi withdrew to hold Beishuo.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi withdrew to hold Beishuo.

sentences.zh: 周將宇文神舉軍逼馬邑，紹義遣杜明達拒之，兵大敗。

translations.literal: Zhou general Yuwen Shenju's army pressed Mayi; Shaoyi sent Du Mingda to resist, and the troops suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou general Yuwen Shenju's army pressed Mayi; Shaoyi sent Du Mingda to resist, and the troops suffered a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 紹義曰：「有死而已，不能降人。

translations.literal: Shaoyi said, "Death is all there is — I cannot surrender to others.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi said, "Death is all there is — I cannot surrender to others.

sentences.zh: 」遂奔突厥。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he fled to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he fled to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 衆三千家，令之曰：「欲還者任意。

translations.literal: Three thousand households followed him; he ordered them, "Whoever wishes to return may do as they please.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand households followed him; he ordered them, "Whoever wishes to return may do as they please.

sentences.zh: 」於是哭拜別者太半。

translations.literal: " More than half wept, bowed, and took leave.
translations.idiomatic: " More than half wept, bowed, and took leave.

sentences.zh: 突厥他缽可汗謂文宣為英雄天子，以紹義重踝似之，甚見愛重，凡齊人在北者，悉隸紹義。

translations.literal: The Turkic Khan Tabo, who called Wenxuan a heroic Son of Heaven, loved and valued Shaoyi because his heavy ankles resembled Wenxuan's; all Qi people in the north were placed under Shaoyi's command.
translations.idiomatic: The Turkic khan Tabo, who called Gao Yang a heroic Son of Heaven, loved and valued Shaoyi because his heavy ankles resembled Gao Yang's; all Qi people in the north were placed under Shaoyi's command.

sentences.zh: 高寶寧在營州，表上尊號，紹義遂卽皇帝位，稱武平元年。

translations.literal: Gao Baoning was at Ying Province and submitted a memorial with an honorific title; Shaoyi thereupon ascended the imperial throne, proclaiming the first year of Wuping.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Baoning was at Ying Province and submitted a memorial with an honorific title; Shaoyi thereupon ascended the imperial throne, proclaiming the first year of Wuping.

sentences.zh: 以趙穆為天水王。

translations.literal: Zhao Mu was made Prince of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Mu was made Prince of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 他缽聞寶寧得平州，亦招諸部，各舉兵南向，云共立范陽王作齊帝，為其報讐。

translations.literal: Tabo heard Baoning had taken Ping Province and also summoned the various tribes, each raising troops southward, declaring they would jointly set up the Prince of Fanyang as Qi emperor and avenge him.
translations.idiomatic: Tabo heard Baoning had taken Ping Province and also summoned the various tribes, each raising troops southward, declaring they would jointly set up the Prince of Fanyang as Qi emperor and avenge him.

sentences.zh: 周武帝大集兵於雲陽，將親北伐，遇疾暴崩。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou massed troops at Yunyang, intending to lead a northern campaign in person, but suddenly died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou massed troops at Yunyang, intending to lead a northern campaign in person, but suddenly died of illness.

sentences.zh: 紹義聞之，以為天贊己。

translations.literal: When Shaoyi heard of it, he thought Heaven was aiding him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyi heard of it, he thought Heaven was aiding him.

sentences.zh: 盧昌斯據范陽，亦表迎紹義。

translations.literal: Lu Changsi held Fanyang and also submitted a memorial welcoming Shaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Changsi held Fanyang and also submitted a memorial welcoming Shaoyi.

sentences.zh: 俄而周將宇文神舉攻滅昌期。

translations.literal: Before long Zhou general Yuwen Shenju attacked and destroyed Changqi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhou general Yuwen Shenju attacked and destroyed Changqi.

sentences.zh: 其日，紹義適至幽州，聞周總管出兵于外，欲乘虛取薊城，列天子旌旗，登燕昭王冢，乘高望遠，部分兵衆。

translations.literal: That day Shaoyi happened to reach You Province; hearing Zhou's military governor had sent troops outward, he wished to take advantage of the vacancy to seize Ji City; he displayed the Son of Heaven's banners and flags, ascended the tomb mound of King Zhao of Yan, and from the height looked far and arrayed his troops.
translations.idiomatic: That day Shaoyi happened to reach You Province; hearing Zhou's military governor had sent troops outward, he wished to take advantage of the vacancy to seize Ji City; he displayed the Son of Heaven's banners and flags, ascended the tomb mound of King Zhao of Yan, and from the height looked far and arrayed his troops.

sentences.zh: 神舉遣大將軍宇文恩將四千人馳救幽州，半為齊軍所殺。

translations.literal: Shenju sent Grand General Yuwen En with four thousand men to ride to relief at You Province; half were killed by Qi troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shenju sent Grand General Yuwen En with four thousand men to ride to relief at You Province; half were killed by Qi troops.

sentences.zh: 紹義聞范陽城陷，素服舉哀，迴軍入突厥。

translations.literal: When Shaoyi heard Fanyang had fallen, he put on plain mourning clothes and wailed; he turned his army and entered the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyi heard Fanyang had fallen, he put on plain mourning clothes and wailed; he turned his army and entered the Turks.

sentences.zh: 周人購之於他缽，又使賀若誼往說之。

translations.literal: Zhou men put a price on his head with Tabo and also sent He Ruoyi to persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou men put a price on his head with Tabo and also sent He Ruoyi to persuade him.

sentences.zh: 他缽猶不忍，遂偽與紹義獵於南境，使誼執之，流于蜀。

translations.literal: Tabo still could not bear to do it; he feigned going hunting with Shaoyi on the southern border and had Ruoyi seize him, then exiled him to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Tabo still could not bear to do it; he feigned going hunting with Shaoyi on the southern border and had Ruoyi seize him, then exiled him to Shu.

sentences.zh: 紹義妃渤海封孝琬女，自突厥逃歸。

translations.literal: Shaoyi's consort, daughter of Feng Xiaowan of Bohai, escaped from the Turks and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi's consort, daughter of Feng Xiaowan of Bohai, escaped from the Turks and returned home.

sentences.zh: 紹義在蜀，遺妃書云：「夷狄無信，送吾於此。

translations.literal: Shaoyi in Shu sent a letter to his consort saying, "The barbarians are faithless — they sent me here.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi in Shu sent a letter to his consort saying, "The barbarians are faithless — they sent me here.

sentences.zh: 」竟死蜀中。

translations.literal: " At last he died in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: " At last he died in Shu.

sentences.zh: 西河王紹仁，文宣第四子也，天保末，為開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Prince Shaoren of Xihe was Wenxuan's fourth son; at the end of Tianbao he was made Opener of the Way with Honors Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shaoren of Xihe was Gao Yang's fourth son; at the end of Tianbao he was made opener of the way with honors equal to the three ducal ministers.

sentences.zh: 尋薨。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 隴西王紹廉，文宣第五子也。

translations.literal: Prince Shaolian of Longxi was Wenxuan's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shaolian of Longxi was Gao Yang's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 初封長樂，後改焉。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed at Changle, later the title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was enfeoffed at Changle, later the title was changed.

sentences.zh: 性粗暴，嘗拔刀逐紹義，紹義走入廄，閉門拒之。

translations.literal: By nature he was violent and rough; once he drew a knife and chased Shaoyi; Shaoyi ran into the stables and shut the door to keep him out.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was violent and rough; once he drew a knife and chased Shaoyi; Shaoyi ran into the stables and shut the door to keep him out.

sentences.zh: 紹義初為清都尹，未及理事，紹廉先往，喚囚悉出，率意決遣之。

translations.literal: When Shaoyi first served as Governor of Qingdu but had not yet taken up affairs, Shaolian went ahead, summoned all prisoners out, and disposed of cases as he saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyi first served as governor of Qingdu but had not yet taken up affairs, Shaolian went ahead, summoned all prisoners out, and disposed of cases as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 能飲酒，一舉數升，終以此薨。

translations.literal: He could drink wine — one draft of several sheng; he ultimately died of it.
translations.idiomatic: He could drink wine — one draft of several sheng; he ultimately died of it.

sentences.zh: 孝昭六王

translations.literal: The Six Princes of Xiaozhao
translations.idiomatic: The Six Princes of Xiaozhao

sentences.zh: 樂陵王百年 始平王彥德 城陽王彥基 定陽王彥康 汝陽王彥忠 汝南王彥理

translations.literal: Prince Bainian of Leiling; Prince Yande of Shiping; Prince Yanji of Chengyang; Prince Yankang of Dingyang; Prince Yanzhong of Ruyang; Prince Yanli of Runan
translations.idiomatic: Prince Bainian of Leiling; Prince Yande of Shiping; Prince Yanji of Chengyang; Prince Yankang of Dingyang; Prince Yanzhong of Ruyang; Prince Yanli of Runan

sentences.zh: 孝昭七男：元后生樂陵王百年，桑氏生襄城王亮，出後襄城景王，諸姬生汝南王彥理、始平王彥德、城陽王彥基、定陽王彥康、汝陽王彥忠。

translations.literal: Xiaozhao had seven sons: the Empress bore Prince Bainian of Leiling; Lady Sang bore Prince Liang of Xiangcheng — who was given in adoption to Prince Jing of Xiangcheng; various ladies bore Prince Yanli of Runan, Prince Yande of Shiping, Prince Yanji of Chengyang, Prince Yankang of Dingyang, and Prince Yanzhong of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yan had seven sons: the empress bore Prince Bainian of Leiling; Lady Sang bore Prince Liang of Xiangcheng — who was given in adoption to Prince Jing of Xiangcheng; various ladies bore Prince Yanli of Runan, Prince Yande of Shiping, Prince Yanji of Chengyang, Prince Yankang of Dingyang, and Prince Yanzhong of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 樂陵王百年，孝昭第二子也。

translations.literal: Prince Bainian of Leiling was Xiaozhao's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Bainian of Leiling was Gao Yan's second son.

sentences.zh: 孝昭初卽位，在晉陽，羣臣請建中宮及太子，帝謙未許，都下百僚又有請，乃稱太后令立為皇太子。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao first ascended, he was at Jinyang; the court ministers requested establishing the empress and crown prince; the emperor modestly did not consent; the officials at the capital again petitioned, and only then, in the empress dowager's name, he was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yan first ascended, he was at Jinyang; the court ministers requested establishing the empress and crown prince; the emperor modestly did not consent; the officials at the capital again petitioned, and only then, in the empress dowager's name, he was established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 帝臨崩，遺詔傳位於武成，並有手書，其末曰：「百年無罪，汝可以樂處置之，勿學前人。

translations.literal: As the emperor faced death, his final edict transferred the throne to Wucheng, and included a handwritten note; at the end it read, "Bainian is without guilt — you may keep him at leisure; do not follow those who came before.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor faced death, his final edict transferred the throne to Gao Zhan, and included a handwritten note; at the end it read, "Bainian is without guilt — you may keep him at leisure; do not follow those who came before.

sentences.zh: 」大寧中，封樂陵王。

translations.literal: " In the Daning era he was enfeoffed Prince of Leiling.
translations.idiomatic: " In the Daning era he was enfeoffed Prince of Leiling.

sentences.zh: 河清三年五月，白虹圍日再重，又橫貫而不達。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Heqing, a white rainbow twice encircled the sun, again stretching across without reaching through.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Heqing, a white rainbow twice encircled the sun, again stretching across without reaching through.

sentences.zh: 赤星見，帝以盆水承星影而蓋之，一夜盆自破。

translations.literal: A red star appeared; the emperor used a basin of water to catch the star's reflection and cover it — in one night the basin broke by itself.
translations.idiomatic: A red star appeared; the emperor used a basin of water to catch the star's reflection and cover it — in one night the basin broke by itself.

sentences.zh: 欲以百年厭之。

translations.literal: He intended to use Bainian to suppress these omens.
translations.idiomatic: He intended to use Bainian to suppress these omens.

sentences.zh: 會博陵人賈德胄教百年書，百年嘗作數「勑」字，德胄封以奏。

translations.literal: It happened that a man of Boling, Jia Dezao, taught Bainian writing; Bainian once wrote several characters for "edict," and Dezao sealed them and submitted the sample.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that a man of Boling, Jia Dezao, taught Bainian writing; Bainian once wrote several characters for "edict," and Dezao sealed them and submitted the sample.

sentences.zh: 帝乃發怒，使召百年。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon flew into rage and had Bainian summoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon flew into rage and had Bainian summoned.

sentences.zh: 百年被召，自知不免，割帶玦留與妃斛律氏。

translations.literal: When Bainian was summoned, knowing he could not escape, he cut off his belt-girdle and pendant and left them for his consort Lady Hulü.
translations.idiomatic: When Bainian was summoned, knowing he could not escape, he cut off his belt-girdle and pendant and left them for his consort Lady Hulü.

sentences.zh: 見帝於玄都苑涼風堂，使百年書「勑」字，驗與德胄所奏相似，遣左右亂捶擊之，又令人曳百年繞堂且走且打，所過處血皆遍地。

translations.literal: He saw the emperor at the Cool Wind Hall in the Xuan Capital Garden; the emperor had Bainian write the character "edict" — it matched what Dezao had submitted — then sent attendants to beat him wildly; others were made to drag Bainian around the hall, beating him as he went; wherever he passed, blood spread across the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He saw the emperor at the Cool Wind Hall in the Xuan Capital Garden; the emperor had Bainian write the character "edict" — it matched what Dezao had submitted — then sent attendants to beat him wildly; others were made to drag Bainian around the hall, beating him as he went; wherever he passed, blood spread across the ground.

sentences.zh: 氣息將盡，曰：「乞命，願與阿叔作奴。

translations.literal: When his breath was nearly gone, he said, "Spare my life — I beg to be your uncle's slave.
translations.idiomatic: When his breath was nearly gone, he said, "Spare my life — I beg to be your uncle's slave.

sentences.zh: 」遂斬之，棄諸池，池水盡赤，於後園親看埋之。

translations.literal: " He was then beheaded and cast into a pool; the pool water turned entirely red; afterward the emperor personally watched as he was buried in the rear garden.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then beheaded and cast into a pool; the pool water turned entirely red; afterward the emperor personally watched as he was buried in the rear garden.

sentences.zh: 妃把玦哀號，不肯食，月餘亦死，玦猶在手，拳不可開，時年十四，其父光自擘之，乃開。

translations.literal: The consort clutched the pendant and wailed, refusing food; after more than a month she too died; the pendant was still in her hand, her fist clenched so it could not be opened; she was fourteen; her father Guang pried it open himself, and only then did it open.
translations.idiomatic: The consort clutched the pendant and wailed, refusing food; after more than a month she too died; the pendant was still in her hand, her fist clenched so it could not be opened; she was fourteen; her father Guang pried it open himself, and only then did it open.

sentences.zh: 後主時，改九院為二十七院，掘得一小屍，緋袍金帶，一髻一解，一足有靴。

translations.literal: In Houzhu's time the nine courtyards were changed to twenty-seven; when digging they found a small corpse in crimson robe and gold belt — one topknot, one unbound, one foot still in boots.
translations.idiomatic: In the Last Emperor's time the nine courtyards were changed to twenty-seven; when digging they found a small corpse in crimson robe and gold belt — one topknot, one unbound, one foot still in boots.

sentences.zh: 諸內參竊言，百年太子也，或言太原王紹德。

translations.literal: The palace attendants whispered among themselves that it was Crown Prince Bainian — or some said Prince Shaode of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The palace attendants whispered among themselves that it was Crown Prince Bainian — or some said Prince Shaode of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 詔以襄成王子白澤襲爵樂陵王。

translations.literal: An edict made Baize, son of the Prince of Xiangcheng, succeed to the title Prince of Leiling.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Baize, son of the Prince of Xiangcheng, succeed to the title Prince of Leiling.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，入關，徙蜀死。

translations.literal: When Qi fell he entered the passes, was transferred to Shu, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he entered the passes, was transferred to Shu, and died there.

sentences.zh: 始平王彥德、城陽王彥基、定陽王彥康、汝陽王彥忠，與汝南同受封，並加儀同三司，後事闕。

translations.literal: Prince Yande of Shiping, Prince Yanji of Chengyang, Prince Yankang of Dingyang, and Prince Yanzhong of Ruyang received enfeoffment together with the Prince of Runan, all additionally given Honors Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers; later events are unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yande of Shiping, Prince Yanji of Chengyang, Prince Yankang of Dingyang, and Prince Yanzhong of Ruyang received enfeoffment together with the Prince of Runan, all additionally given honors equal to the three ducal ministers; later events are unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 武成十二王

translations.literal: The Twelve Princes of Wucheng
translations.idiomatic: The Twelve Princes of Wucheng

sentences.zh: 南陽王綽 琅邪王儼 齊安王廓 北平王貞

translations.literal: Prince Chuo of Nanyang; Prince Yan of Langye; Prince Kuo of Qi'an; Prince Zhen of Beiping
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chuo of Nanyang; Prince Yan of Langye; Prince Kuo of Qi'an; Prince Zhen of Beiping

sentences.zh: 高平王仁英 淮南王仁光 西河王仁幾 樂平王仁邕

translations.literal: Prince Renying of Gaoping; Prince Renguang of Huainan; Prince Renji of Xihe; Prince Renyong of Leping
translations.idiomatic: Prince Renying of Gaoping; Prince Renguang of Huainan; Prince Renji of Xihe; Prince Renyong of Leping

sentences.zh: 潁川王仁儉 安陽王仁雅 丹陽王仁直 東海王仁謙

translations.literal: Prince Renjian of Yingchuan; Prince Renya of Anyang; Prince Renzhi of Danyang; Prince Renqian of Donghai
translations.idiomatic: Prince Renjian of Yingchuan; Prince Renya of Anyang; Prince Renzhi of Danyang; Prince Renqian of Donghai

sentences.zh: 武成十三男：胡皇后生後主及琅邪王儼，李夫人生南陽王綽，後宮生齊安王廓、北平王貞、高平王仁英、淮南王仁光、西河王仁幾、樂平王仁邕、潁川王仁儉、安樂王仁雅、丹陽王仁直、東海王仁謙。

translations.literal: Wucheng had thirteen sons: Empress Hu bore Houzhu and Prince Yan of Langye; Lady Li bore Prince Chuo of Nanyang; the rear palace bore Prince Kuo of Qi'an, Prince Zhen of Beiping, Prince Renying of Gaoping, Prince Renguang of Huainan, Prince Renji of Xihe, Prince Renyong of Leping, Prince Renjian of Yingchuan, Prince Renya of Anle, Prince Renzhi of Danyang, and Prince Renqian of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhan had thirteen sons: Empress Hu bore the Last Emperor and Prince Yan of Langye; Lady Li bore Prince Chuo of Nanyang; the rear palace bore Prince Kuo of Qi'an, Prince Zhen of Beiping, Prince Renying of Gaoping, Prince Renguang of Huainan, Prince Renji of Xihe, Prince Renyong of Leping, Prince Renjian of Yingchuan, Prince Renya of Anle, Prince Renzhi of Danyang, and Prince Renqian of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 南陽王綽，字仁通，武成長子也。

translations.literal: Prince Chuo of Nanyang, styled Rentong, was Wucheng's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chuo of Nanyang, styled Rentong, was Gao Zhan's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 以五月五日辰時生，至午時，後主乃生。

translations.literal: Born at the fifth hour of the fifth day of the fifth month; only at the noon hour was Houzhu born.
translations.idiomatic: Born at the fifth hour of the fifth day of the fifth month; only at the noon hour was the Last Emperor born.

sentences.zh: 武成以綽母李夫人非正嫡，故貶為第二，初名融，字君明，出後漢陽王。

translations.literal: Wucheng, because Chuo's mother Lady Li was not the legitimate consort, demoted him to second rank; his original name was Rong, styled Junming; he was given in adoption to the Prince of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhan, because Chuo's mother Lady Li was not the legitimate consort, demoted him to second rank; his original name was Rong, styled Junming; he was given in adoption to the Prince of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 河清三年，改封南陽，別為漢陽置後。

translations.literal: In the third year of Heqing the title was changed to Prince of Nanyang, and a separate heir was established for Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Heqing the title was changed to Prince of Nanyang, and a separate heir was established for Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 綽始十餘歲，留守晉陽。

translations.literal: When Chuo was barely past ten he remained at Jinyang on guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuo was barely past ten he remained at Jinyang on guard duty.

sentences.zh: 愛波斯狗，尉破胡諫之，欻然斫殺數狗，狼藉在地。

translations.literal: He loved Persian dogs; Wei Pohuo remonstrated with him; instantly he hacked several dogs to death — their corpses strewn across the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He loved Persian dogs; Wei Pohuo remonstrated with him; instantly he hacked several dogs to death — their corpses strewn across the ground.

sentences.zh: 破胡驚走，不敢復言。

translations.literal: Pohuo fled in shock and dared speak no more.
translations.idiomatic: Pohuo fled in shock and dared speak no more.

sentences.zh: 後為司徒、冀州刺史，好裸人，使踞為獸狀，縱犬噬而食之。

translations.literal: Later he served as Minister of Works and Governor of Ji Province; he liked to strip people naked, make them crouch in the shape of beasts, and set dogs on them to devour the flesh.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as minister of works and governor of Ji Province; he liked to strip people naked, make them crouch in the shape of beasts, and set dogs on them to devour the flesh.

sentences.zh: 左轉定州，汲井水為後池，在樓上彈人。

translations.literal: Transferred left to Ding Province — he drew well water for a rear pool and from the tower shot at people.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred left to Ding Province — he drew well water for a rear pool and from the tower shot at people.

sentences.zh: 好微行，遊獵無度，恣情強暴，云學文宣伯為人。

translations.literal: He loved going about incognito, hunting without limit, indulging in violence at will — saying he was studying Duke Wenxuan's conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He loved going about incognito, hunting without limit, indulging in violence at will — saying he was studying Gao Yang's conduct.

sentences.zh: 有婦人抱兒在路，走避入草，綽奪其兒飼波斯狗。

translations.literal: A woman carrying a child was on the road; running to hide in the grass — Chuo snatched her child and fed it to his Persian dog.
translations.idiomatic: A woman carrying a child was on the road; running to hide in the grass — Chuo snatched her child and fed it to his Persian dog.

sentences.zh: 婦人號哭，綽怒，又縱狗使食，狗不食，塗以兒血，乃食焉。

translations.literal: The woman shrieked and wept; Chuo in anger set the dog on her to eat as well; the dog would not eat; smearing the child's blood on her, then it ate.
translations.idiomatic: The woman shrieked and wept; Chuo in anger set the dog on her to eat as well; the dog would not eat; smearing the child's blood on her, then it ate.

sentences.zh: 後主聞之，詔鎖綽赴行在所。

translations.literal: When Houzhu heard of it, he issued an edict to lock Chuo up and send him to the imperial traveling encampment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor heard of it, he issued an edict to lock Chuo up and send him to the imperial traveling encampment.

sentences.zh: 至而宥之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 問在州何者最樂，對曰：「多取蠍將蛆混，看極樂。

translations.literal: Asked what at the province gave greatest pleasure, he replied, "Taking many scorpions and mixing them with maggots — watching them is supreme delight.
translations.idiomatic: Asked what at the province gave greatest pleasure, he replied, "Taking many scorpions and mixing them with maggots — watching them is supreme delight.

sentences.zh: 」後主卽夜索蠍一斗，比曉得三二升，置諸浴斛，使人裸臥斛中，號叫宛轉。

translations.literal: " That very night Houzhu sent for a peck of scorpions; by dawn he had gathered only two or three sheng; they were placed in a bathing tub and a man was made to lie naked in it, crying out in agony.
translations.idiomatic: " That very night the Last Emperor sent for a peck of scorpions; by dawn he had gathered only two or three sheng; they were placed in a bathing tub and a man was made to lie naked in it, crying out in agony.

sentences.zh: 帝與綽臨觀，喜噱不已，謂綽曰：「如此樂事，何不早馳驛奏聞。

translations.literal: The emperor and Chuo watched and laughed without end, saying to Chuo, "Such a delightful sport — why didn't you report it by urgent post earlier?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and Chuo watched and laughed without end, saying to Chuo, "Such a delightful sport — why didn't you report it by urgent post earlier?

sentences.zh: 」綽由是大為後主寵，拜大將軍，朝夕同戲。

translations.literal: " Chuo on this account came into great favor with Houzhu; he was appointed Grand General and sported with him morning and night.
translations.idiomatic: " Chuo on this account came into great favor with the Last Emperor; he was appointed grand general and sported with him morning and night.

sentences.zh: 韓長鸞間之，除齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Han Changluan heard of it and had him transferred out as Governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Han Changluan heard of it and had him transferred out as governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 將發，長鸞令綽親信誣告其反，奏云：「此犯國法，不可赦。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, Changluan had Chuo's trusted men falsely accuse him of rebellion and memorialized, "This violates the laws of the state and cannot be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart, Changluan had Chuo's trusted men falsely accuse him of rebellion and memorialized, "This violates the laws of the state and cannot be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 」後主不忍顯戮，使寵胡何猥薩後園與綽相撲，搤殺之。

translations.literal: " Houzhu could not bear to execute him publicly; he had the favored Hun attendant He Weisa wrestle with Chuo in the rear garden and strangle him to death.
translations.idiomatic: " The Last Emperor could not bear to execute him publicly; he had the favored Hun attendant He Weisa wrestle with Chuo in the rear garden and strangle him to death.

sentences.zh: 瘞於興聖佛寺。

translations.literal: He was buried at the Xingsheng Buddhist Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at Xingsheng Temple.

sentences.zh: 經四百餘日乃大斂，顏色毛發皆如生，俗云五月五日生者腦不壞。

translations.literal: After more than four hundred days a great interment was finally performed; his complexion and hair were all as if alive. Popular lore says those born on the fifth day of the fifth month do not suffer decay of the brain.
translations.idiomatic: More than four hundred days passed before he received full burial; his complexion and hair looked as if he were still alive. Folk wisdom holds that those born on the fifth day of the fifth month never rot above the neck.

sentences.zh: 綽兄弟皆呼父為兄兄，嫡母為家家，乳母為姊姊，婦為妹妹。

translations.literal: Chuo's brothers all called their father elder brother, their principal mother mother dear, their wet nurse elder sister, and their wives little sister.
translations.idiomatic: Among Chuo's brothers, all called their father "Elder Brother," the principal mother "Mother Dear," the wet nurse "Elder Sister," and their wives "Little Sister."

sentences.zh: 齊亡，妃鄭氏為周武帝所幸，請葬綽。

translations.literal: When Qi perished, his consort Lady Zheng, whom Emperor Wu of Zhou favored, requested burial for Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell, his consort Lady Zheng — a favorite of Emperor Wu of Zhou — petitioned for Chuo's burial.

sentences.zh: 勑所司葬於永平陵北。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to bury him north of Yongping Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him buried north of Yongping Tomb.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王儼，字仁威，武成第三子也。

translations.literal: Prince Yan of Langya, courtesy name Renwei, was Wucheng's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yan of Langya, courtesy name Renwei, was Gao Zhan's third son.

sentences.zh: 初封東平王，拜開府、侍中、中書監、京畿大都督、領軍大將軍、領御史中丞，遷司徒、尚書令、大將軍、錄尚書事、大司馬。

translations.literal: Initially enfeoffed Prince of Dongping, he was appointed opening-establishment grand master, attendant within the palace, supervisor of the Secretariat, metropolitan governor of the capital region, grand general commanding the imperial guard, and concurrently imperial censor-in-chief; he was transferred to minister over the masses, chief minister of the Masters of Writing, grand general, recorder of affairs of the Masters of Writing, and grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Initially enfeoffed Prince of Dongping, he received posts as opening-establishment grand master, palace attendant, Secretariat supervisor, metropolitan governor of the capital region, commander of the imperial guard and concurrent imperial censor-in-chief; later he rose to minister over the masses, chief minister of the Masters of Writing, grand general, recorder of the Masters of Writing, and grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 魏氏舊制，中丞出，清道，與皇太子分路行，王公皆遙住車，去牛，頓軛於地，以待中丞過，其或遲違，則赤棒棒之。

translations.literal: Under the old Wei system, when the censor-in-chief went out the route was cleared; he and the crown prince traveled by separate roads. Princes and nobles all halted their carriages at a distance, removed their oxen, set the yokes on the ground, and waited for the censor to pass; if anyone was tardy or disobedient, red clubs struck him.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old Wei rule, when the censor-in-chief went abroad the road was cleared and he and the crown prince used separate routes. Princes and nobles all stopped their carriages at a distance, unhitched the oxen, laid the yokes on the ground, and waited for the censor to pass; tardiness or disobedience brought blows from red clubs.

sentences.zh: 自都鄴後，此儀浸絕，武成欲雄寵儼，乃使一依舊制。

translations.literal: After the capital moved to Ye this ceremony had gradually died out; Wucheng, wishing to magnify Yan's favor, had it restored in full according to the old statute.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital moved to Ye this ceremony had faded; Gao Zhan, wanting to exalt Yan's position, restored it entirely to the old form.

sentences.zh: 初從北宮出，將上中丞，凡京畿步騎，領軍之官屬，中丞之威儀，司徒之鹵簿，莫不畢備。

translations.literal: The first time he left the Northern Palace to assume his duties as censor-in-chief, all the infantry and cavalry of the capital region, the staff of the army commander, the censor's full retinue, and the minister's ceremonial guard were completely provided.
translations.idiomatic: The first time he left the Northern Palace to take up the censorate, the capital infantry and cavalry, the commander's entire staff, the censor's full retinue, and the minister's ceremonial escort were all deployed without exception.

sentences.zh: 帝與胡后在華林園東門外張幕，隔青紗步障觀之。

translations.literal: The emperor and Empress Hu spread a canopy outside the east gate of Hualin Garden and watched from behind a green gauze screen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and Empress Hu set a pavilion outside the east gate of Hualin Garden and watched from behind a green gauze screen.

sentences.zh: 遣中貴驟馬趣仗，不得入，自言奉勑，赤棒應聲碎其鞍，馬驚人墜。

translations.literal: He sent a palace eunuch galloping to the guard formation; entry was refused. Declaring he came by imperial order, red clubs instantly smashed his saddle; the horse bolted and the man fell.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a palace eunuch galloping toward the guard line; they would not admit him. Claiming an imperial order, he was answered by red clubs that smashed his saddle — the horse bolted and he fell.

sentences.zh: 帝大笑，以為善。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed greatly and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed heartily and approved.

sentences.zh: 更勑令駐車，傳語良久，觀者傾京邑。

translations.literal: He issued another order to halt the carriage and converse at length; spectators filled the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Another order kept the carriage halted while messages passed back and forth at length; onlookers filled the capital.

sentences.zh: 儼恒在宮中，坐含光殿以視事，諸父皆拜焉。

translations.literal: Yan constantly remained in the palace, holding court from Han'guang Hall; all his uncles bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan lived constantly in the palace, conducting affairs from Han'guang Hall; all his uncles bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 帝幸幷州，儼常居守，每送駕，或半路，或至晉陽，乃還。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Bing Province, Yan usually stayed behind as regent; each time he escorted the imperial procession, he would turn back halfway or only after reaching Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Bing Province, Yan usually remained as regent; each farewell escort ended halfway, or only after Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 王師羅常從駕，後至，武成欲罪之，辭曰：「臣與第三子別，留連不覺晚。

translations.literal: Wang Shiluo often accompanied the imperial train and arrived late; Wucheng wished to punish him. He pleaded, "Your servant parted from the Third Son and lingered without noticing how late it had grown.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiluo often rode with the imperial train and once arrived late; Gao Zhan meant to punish him. He pleaded, "Your servant took leave of the Third Son and lingered without noticing how late it had grown.

sentences.zh: 」武成憶儼，為之下泣，舍師羅不問。

translations.literal: " Wucheng thought of Yan and wept; he pardoned Shiluo without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Zhan thought of Yan and wept; he pardoned Shiluo without further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 儼器服玩飾，皆與後主同，所須悉官給。

translations.literal: Yan's vessels, robes, toys, and ornaments all matched the Last Emperor's; everything he wanted was supplied by official requisition.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's vessels, robes, ornaments, and playthings all matched Houzhu's; whatever he wanted the court supplied.

sentences.zh: 於南宮嘗見新冰早李，還，怒曰：「尊兄已有，我何意無！

translations.literal: Once at the Southern Palace he saw early plums chilled with ice. Returning, he cried in anger, "Elder Brother already has them — why should I go without!
translations.idiomatic: Once at the Southern Palace he saw ice-chilled early plums. Returning, he raged: "Elder Brother already has them — why should I have none!

sentences.zh: 」從是，後主先得新奇，屬官及工匠必獲罪。

translations.literal: " From then on Houzhu always received novelties first; any attendant or craftsman who failed to understand this was punished.
translations.idiomatic: " After that Houzhu always received novelties first; any attendant or craftsman who missed the point was punished.

sentences.zh: 太上、胡后猶以為不足。

translations.literal: Even the Retired Emperor and Empress Hu considered this insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Even the retired emperor and Empress Hu thought this still not enough.

sentences.zh: 儼常患喉，使醫下針，張目不瞬。

translations.literal: Yan often suffered sore throat; when the physician needled him, he kept his eyes open without blinking.
translations.idiomatic: Yan often had a sore throat; when a physician needled him he never blinked.

sentences.zh: 又言於帝曰：「阿兄懦，何能率左右？

translations.literal: He also told the emperor, "Elder Brother is timid — how could he command those around him?
translations.idiomatic: He told the emperor, "Elder Brother is soft — how could he command those around him?

sentences.zh: 」帝每稱曰：「此黠兒也，當有所成。

translations.literal: " The emperor always praised him: "This clever boy will surely achieve something.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor always said, "This sharp boy will amount to something.

sentences.zh: 」以後主為劣，有廢立意。

translations.literal: " Holding Houzhu inferior, he had thoughts of deposing him.
translations.idiomatic: " Thinking Houzhu inferior, he entertained thoughts of deposing him.

sentences.zh: 武成崩，改封琅邪。

translations.literal: After Wucheng died, Yan's title was changed to Langya.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Zhan died, Yan's title was changed to Langya.

sentences.zh: 儼以和土開、駱提婆等奢恣，盛修第宅，意甚不平，嘗謂曰：「君等所營宅早晚當就，何太遲也。

translations.literal: Yan resented He Shikai, Luotipo, and the rest for their extravagant indulgence and grand house-building, and once said to them, "The houses you are building must be finished soon — why so slow?
translations.idiomatic: Yan resented He Shikai, Luotipo, and the rest for their extravagance and grand house-building. Once he said, "The mansions you are raising will be finished soon enough — why so slow?

sentences.zh: 」二人相謂曰：「琅邪王眼光奕奕，數步射人，向者暫對，不覺汗出，天子前奏事尚不然。

translations.literal: " The two said to each other, "The Prince of Langya's eyes blaze — even at a few paces they pierce a man. Just now facing him briefly, we broke into a sweat without noticing; before the Son of Heaven in audience it is not even so.
translations.idiomatic: " The two said to each other, "Prince Yan's eyes blaze — at a few paces they bore into you. That brief meeting left us sweating before we knew it; even before the emperor in audience it is not so.

sentences.zh: 」由是忌之。

translations.literal: " From this they came to fear him.
translations.idiomatic: " From this they came to fear him.

sentences.zh: 武平二年，出儼居北宮，五日一朝，不復得每日見太后。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wuping he was sent to live in the Northern Palace; he attended court toward the empress dowager only once every five days and no longer saw her daily.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wuping he was moved to the Northern Palace; he attended court toward the empress dowager only once every five days and no longer saw her daily.

sentences.zh: 四月，詔除太保，餘官悉解，猶帶中丞，督京畿。

translations.literal: In the fourth month an edict removed him as grand preceptor while all other offices were stripped; he retained only the censorate and oversight of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month an edict removed him as grand preceptor and stripped every other office; he kept only the censorate and oversight of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 以北城有武庫，欲移儼於外，然後奪其兵權。

translations.literal: Since the northern city held an armory, they wished to move Yan outside before stripping him of military authority.
translations.idiomatic: Because the northern city held the armory, they intended to move Yan outside first, then seize his military authority.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史王子宜與儼左右開府高舍洛、中常侍劉辟疆說儼曰：「殿下被疏，正由士開間構，何可出北宮入百姓叢中也。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Wang Ziyi and Yan's attendants, opening-establishment officer Gao Shelou and palace attendant Liu Biqiang, urged Yan: "Your Highness has been pushed aside precisely because Shikai sowed discord — how can you leave the Northern Palace and enter the common throng?
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Wang Ziyi and Yan's attendants Gao Shelou and Liu Biqiang urged him: "You have been sidelined because Shikai stirred up trouble — how can you leave the Northern Palace and walk among common people?

sentences.zh: 」儼謂侍中馮子琮曰：「士開罪重，兒欲殺之。

translations.literal: " Yan told attendant Feng Zicong, "Shikai's crimes are grave — I wish to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan told attendant Feng Zicong, "Shikai's crimes are grave — I mean to kill him.

sentences.zh: 」子琮心欲廢帝而立儼，因贊成其事。

translations.literal: " Zicong inwardly wished to depose the emperor and enthrone Yan, and so encouraged the plan.
translations.idiomatic: " Zicong inwardly wanted to depose the emperor and enthrone Yan, and egged him on.

sentences.zh: 儼乃令子宜表彈士開罪，請付禁推。

translations.literal: Yan then had Ziyi submit an impeachment of Shikai's crimes, requesting detention and interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had Ziyi submit an impeachment of Shikai's crimes, asking that he be taken into custody and investigated.

sentences.zh: 子琮雜以他文書奏之，後主不審省而可之。

translations.literal: Zicong mixed other documents into the memorial; the Last Emperor did not examine it closely and approved.
translations.idiomatic: Zicong mixed other papers into the memorial; Houzhu did not read closely and approved.

sentences.zh: 儼誑領軍厙狄伏連曰：「奉勑令軍收士開。

translations.literal: Yan deceived army commander Kudi Fulian, saying, "By imperial order you are to seize Shikai.
translations.idiomatic: Yan deceived army commander Kudi Fulian: "By imperial order, take Shikai.

sentences.zh: 」伏連以咨子琮，且請覆奏。

translations.literal: " Fulian consulted Zicong and asked to confirm the order with another memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " Fulian consulted Zicong and asked to confirm the order by memorial.

sentences.zh: 子琮曰：「琅邪王受勑，何須重奏。

translations.literal: Zicong said, "The Prince of Langya bears the order — what need to memorialize again?
translations.idiomatic: Zicong said, "Prince Yan already holds the order — why memorialize again?

sentences.zh: 」伏連信之，伏五十人於神獸門外，詰旦，執士開送御史。

translations.literal: " Fulian believed him, hid fifty men outside the Divine Beast Gate, and at dawn seized Shikai and delivered him to the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: " Fulian believed him, hid fifty men outside the Divine Beast Gate, and at dawn seized Shikai and sent him to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 儼使馮永洛就臺斬之。

translations.literal: Yan sent Feng Yongluo to the office and had Shikai beheaded on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent Feng Yongluo to the censorate and had Shikai beheaded there.

sentences.zh: 儼徒本意唯殺士開，及是，因逼儼曰：「事既然，不可中止。

translations.literal: Yan's followers had intended only to kill Shikai; once that was done they pressed Yan: "The deed is done — there can be no turning back.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's men had meant only to kill Shikai; once it was done they pressed him: "The thing is started — it cannot stop now.

sentences.zh: 」儼遂率京畿軍士三千餘人屯千秋門。

translations.literal: " Yan then led more than three thousand capital-region soldiers and encamped at Qianqiu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan then led more than three thousand capital soldiers and encamped at Qianqiu Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝使劉桃枝將禁兵八十人召儼。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Liu Taozhi with eighty palace troops to summon Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Liu Taozhi with eighty palace troops to summon Yan.

sentences.zh: 桃枝遙拜，儼命反縛，將斬之，禁兵散走。

translations.literal: Taozhi bowed from afar; Yan ordered him bound hand and foot for execution; the palace troops scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Taozhi bowed from a distance; Yan ordered him bound for beheading; the palace troops fled.

sentences.zh: 帝又使馮子琮召儼，儼辭曰：「士開昔來實合萬死，謀廢至尊，剃家家頭使作阿尼，故擁兵馬欲坐著孫鳳珍宅上，臣為是矯詔誅之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Feng Zicong to summon Yan. Yan refused, saying, "Shikai deserved ten thousand deaths — he plotted to depose His Majesty, shave Mother Dear's head and make her a nun, and therefore amassed troops to seize Sun Fengzhen's house; for this Your Servant falsified an order and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Feng Zicong again. Yan refused: "Shikai deserved death many times over — he plotted to depose the emperor, shave Mother Dear's head and make her a nun, and amassed troops to seize Sun Fengzhen's mansion; I falsified an order and killed him for that.

sentences.zh: 尊兄若欲殺臣，不敢逃罪，若放臣，願遣姊姊來迎臣，臣卽入見。

translations.literal: If Elder Brother wishes to kill me I will not flee guilt; if he spares me, send Elder Sister to fetch me and I will enter at once.
translations.idiomatic: If Elder Brother wishes to kill me I will not flee my guilt; if he spares me, let Elder Sister come fetch me and I will enter at once.

sentences.zh: 」姊姊卽陸令萱也，儼欲誘出殺之。

translations.literal: " Elder Sister was Lu Lingxuan; Yan intended to lure her out and kill her.
translations.idiomatic: " "Elder Sister" was Lu Lingxuan — Yan meant to lure her out and kill her.

sentences.zh: 令萱執刀帝後，聞之戰栗。

translations.literal: Lingxuan stood behind the emperor with a knife in hand; hearing this, she trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxuan stood behind the emperor with a knife; hearing this, she trembled.

sentences.zh: 又使韓長鸞召儼，儼將入，劉辟疆牽衣諫曰：「若不斬提婆母子，殿下無由得入。

translations.literal: Han Changluan was sent to summon Yan again. As Yan was about to enter, Liu Biqiang seized his robe and remonstrated: "Unless you cut down the Tipo mother and son, Your Highness has no way inside.
translations.idiomatic: Han Changluan was sent again. As Yan was about to enter, Liu Biqiang seized his robe: "Unless you kill Tipo and his mother, Your Highness cannot get in.

sentences.zh: 」廣寧、安德二王適從西來，欲助成其事，曰：「何不入？

translations.literal: " Princes Guangning and Ande had just come from the west and wished to help the cause. They said, "Why not go in?
translations.idiomatic: " Princes Guangning and Ande had just arrived from the west and wanted to help. They said, "Why not go in?

sentences.zh: 」辟疆曰：「人少。

translations.literal: " Biqiang said, "Our numbers are too few.
translations.idiomatic: " Biqiang said, "We are too few.

sentences.zh: 」安德王顧衆而言曰：「孝昭帝殺楊遵彥，止八十人，今乃數千，何言人少？

translations.literal: " Prince Ande looked at the crowd and said, "When Emperor Xiaozhao killed Yang Zunyan it took only eighty men — now there are thousands; why say too few?
translations.idiomatic: " Prince Ande looked at the host and said, "When Emperor Gao Yan killed Yang Zunyan it took only eighty men — now we are thousands; how can we be too few?

sentences.zh: 」後主泣啟太后曰：「有緣更見家家，無緣永別。

translations.literal: " The Last Emperor wept and told the empress dowager, "If fate allows I may see Mother Dear again; if not, this is eternal parting.
translations.idiomatic: " Houzhu wept to the empress dowager: "If fate allows I may see Mother Dear again; if not, this is farewell forever.

sentences.zh: 」乃急召斛律光，儼亦召之。

translations.literal: " They hastily summoned Hulu Guang; Yan summoned him too.
translations.idiomatic: " They hastily summoned Hulu Guang; Yan summoned him as well.

sentences.zh: 光聞殺士開，撫掌大笑曰：「龍子作事，固自不似凡人。

translations.literal: Guang heard Shikai had been killed, clapped his hands and laughed: "A dragon's son does business — naturally not like ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: Guang heard Shikai was dead, clapped his hands and laughed: "A dragon's son at work — of course not like ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 」入見後主於永巷。

translations.literal: " He entered to see the emperor in Yong Lane.
translations.idiomatic: " He entered and saw the emperor in Yong Lane.

sentences.zh: 帝率宿衛者步騎四百，授甲將出戰。

translations.literal: The emperor led four hundred palace guards on foot and horseback, armed for battle, preparing to sortie.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor led four hundred palace guards, armed for battle, preparing to sortie.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「小兒輩弄兵，與交手卽亂。

translations.literal: Guang said, "These little fellows playing with weapons — grapple with them and all turns to chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "Boys playing soldier — clash with them and everything turns to chaos.

sentences.zh: 鄙諺雲『奴見大家心死』，至尊宜自至千秋門，琅邪必不敢動。

translations.literal: A vulgar proverb runs, 'When a slave sees the master his heart dies.' Your Majesty should go to Qianqiu Gate yourself; Langya will surely not stir.
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says, 'When a slave sees the master his heart dies.' Your Majesty should go to Qianqiu Gate yourself; Langya dare not move.

sentences.zh: 」皮景和亦以為然，後主從之。

translations.literal: " Pi Jinghe also agreed; the Last Emperor followed their advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Pi Jinghe agreed; Houzhu took their counsel.

sentences.zh: 光步道，使人出曰：「大家來。

translations.literal: Guang walked ahead and had a man call out, "The master comes.
translations.idiomatic: Guang walked ahead and had a man shout, "The master comes.

sentences.zh: 」儼徒駭散。

translations.literal: " Yan's followers panicked and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan's followers panicked and scattered.

sentences.zh: 帝駐馬橋上，遙呼之，儼猶立不進。

translations.literal: The emperor halted his horse on the bridge and called from afar; Yan still stood without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor halted on the bridge and shouted from afar; Yan still would not move.

sentences.zh: 光就謂曰：「天子弟殺一漢，何所苦。

translations.literal: Guang went to him and said, "The emperor's brother killed one Han — what hardship is that?
translations.idiomatic: Guang went to him: "The emperor's brother killed one Han — what's the hardship in that?

sentences.zh: 」執其手，強引以前。

translations.literal: " He seized Yan's hand and forcibly pulled him forward.
translations.idiomatic: " He seized Yan's hand and dragged him forward.

sentences.zh: 請帝曰：「琅邪王年少，腸肥腦滿，輕為舉措，長大自不復然，願寬其罪。

translations.literal: He pleaded with the emperor: "The Prince of Langya is young — fat of belly and full of brains, he acts rashly; when he grows he will not again. I beg his crime be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded with the emperor: "Prince Yan is young — thick-waisted and rash; grown, he will not act so again. I beg you pardon him.

sentences.zh: 」帝拔儼帶刀環亂築辮頭，良久乃釋之。

translations.literal: " The emperor snatched Yan's sword-ring and beat his braided hair with it at random; only after a long while did he release him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor snatched Yan's sword-ring and beat his braided hair with it for a long while before letting him go.

sentences.zh: 收伏連及高舍洛、王子宜、劉辟疆、都督翟顯貴於後園，帝親射之而後斬，皆支解，暴之都街下。

translations.literal: Fulian, Gao Shelou, Wang Ziyi, Liu Biqiang, and commander Zhai Xiankui were seized in the rear garden; the emperor shot them personally and then had them beheaded, all dismembered and exposed beneath the capital's street.
translations.idiomatic: Fulian, Gao Shelou, Wang Ziyi, Liu Biqiang, and commander Zhai Xiankui were seized in the rear garden; the emperor shot them himself, then had them beheaded, dismembered, and exposed in the capital streets.

sentences.zh: 文武職吏盡欲殺之。

translations.literal: The civil and military officers all wanted them killed.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officers all wanted them killed.

sentences.zh: 光以皆勳貴子弟，恐人心不安，趙彥深亦云《春秋》責帥，於是罪之各有差。

translations.literal: Guang said that since all were sons of meritorious nobles, fearing unrest among hearts, Zhao Yanshen also cited the Spring and Autumn Annals that blame falls on the commander — and so punishments were graded accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said they were all sons of meritorious houses and feared unrest; Zhao Yanshen also cited the Spring and Autumn principle that blame falls on the commander — and sentences were graded accordingly.

sentences.zh: 儼之未獲罪也，鄴北城有白馬佛塔，是石季龍為澄公所作，儼將修之。

translations.literal: Before Yan yet fell under guilt, north of Ye there was a white-horse pagoda built by Shi Jilong for Master Cheng; Yan was about to repair it.
translations.idiomatic: Before Yan was punished, north of Ye stood a white-horse pagoda that Shi Jilong had built for Master Cheng; Yan meant to restore it.

sentences.zh: 巫曰：「若動此浮圖，北城失主。

translations.literal: A shaman said, "If this stupa is moved, the northern city will lose its lord.
translations.idiomatic: A shaman said, "Move this stupa and the northern city loses its master.

sentences.zh: 」不從，破至第二級，得白蛇長數丈，回旋失之，數旬而敗。

translations.literal: " He did not listen; breaking through to the second tier they found a white serpent several zhang long, which coiled away and vanished; within ten-odd days came defeat.
translations.idiomatic: " He ignored the warning; breaking through to the second tier they found a white serpent several zhang long that coiled away and vanished — within ten-odd days came defeat.

sentences.zh: 自是太后處儼於宮內，食必自嘗之。

translations.literal: From then the empress dowager kept Yan within the palace and always tasted his food herself.
translations.idiomatic: From then the empress dowager kept Yan in the palace and tasted every meal herself.

sentences.zh: 陸令萱說帝曰：「人稱琅邪王聰明雄勇，當今無敵，觀其相表，殆非人臣。

translations.literal: Lu Lingxuan said to the emperor, "People call the Prince of Langya clever and bold, unmatched today; judging his countenance, he scarcely seems fit to be a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Lingxuan told the emperor, "People say Prince Yan is clever and bold, a match for no one today; his face scarcely looks like a subject's.

sentences.zh: 自專殺以來，常懷恐懼，宜早為計。

translations.literal: Since the unauthorized killing he has lived in constant fear; one should plan early.
translations.idiomatic: Since the killing he has lived in fear — better plan early.

sentences.zh: 」何洪珍與和士開素善，亦請殺之。

translations.literal: " He Hongzhen, who was always on good terms with He Shikai, also asked that Yan be killed.
translations.idiomatic: " He Hongzhen, always close to He Shikai, also urged Yan's death.

sentences.zh: 未決，以食輿密迎祖珽問之，珽稱周公誅管叔，季友鴆慶父，帝納其言。

translations.literal: Undecided, they secretly sent a food carriage to fetch Zu Ting and ask him; Ting cited the Duke of Zhou's execution of Guan Shu and Ji You's poisoning of Qing Fu; the emperor accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Still undecided, they secretly sent a food carriage for Zu Ting; he cited the Duke of Zhou executing Guan Shu and Ji You poisoning Duke Qing's killer; the emperor accepted this.

sentences.zh: 以儼之晉陽，使右衛大將軍趙元侃誘執儼。

translations.literal: When Yan was sent to Jinyang, Right Guard grand general Zhao Yuankan was made to lure and seize him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was sent to Jinyang, right guard grand general Zhao Yuankan was told to lure and seize him.

sentences.zh: 元侃曰：「臣昔事先帝，日見先帝愛王，今寧就死，不能行。

translations.literal: Yuankan said, "Your servant once served the late emperor and daily saw how he loved the prince; now I would rather die than do this.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankan said, "I once served the late emperor and saw daily how he loved this prince; I would rather die than do this now.

sentences.zh: 」帝出元侃為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: " The emperor sent Yuankan out as governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent Yuankan away as governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 九月下旬，帝啟太后曰：「明旦欲與仁威出獵，須早出早還。

translations.literal: In the last ten days of the ninth month the emperor told the empress dowager, "Tomorrow I wish to hunt with Renwei, leaving early and returning early.
translations.idiomatic: In the last ten days of the ninth month the emperor told the empress dowager, "Tomorrow I hunt with Renwei — out early, back early.

sentences.zh: 」是夜四更，帝召儼，儼疑之。

translations.literal: " That night at the fourth watch the emperor summoned Yan; Yan was suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: " That night at the fourth watch the emperor summoned Yan; Yan was suspicious.

sentences.zh: 陸令萱曰：「兄兄喚，兒何不去？

translations.literal: Lu Lingxuan said, "Elder Brother calls — why will you not go?
translations.idiomatic: Lu Lingxuan said, "Elder Brother calls — why won't you go?

sentences.zh: 」儼出至永巷，劉桃枝反接其手。

translations.literal: " Yan went out to Yong Lane; Liu Taozhi bound his hands behind him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan went out to Yong Lane; Liu Taozhi bound his hands behind his back.

sentences.zh: 儼呼曰：「乞見家家、尊兄！

translations.literal: Yan cried out, "I beg to see Mother Dear and Elder Brother!
translations.idiomatic: Yan cried, "Let me see Mother Dear and Elder Brother!

sentences.zh: 」桃枝以袂塞其口，反袍蒙頭負出，至大明宮，鼻血滿面，立殺之，時年十四。

translations.literal: " Taozhi stuffed his mouth with his sleeve, hooded his head in the reversed robe, and carried him out; at Daming Palace his nose bled over his face and he was immediately killed — aged fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: " Taozhi stuffed his mouth with his sleeve, covered his head in the reversed robe, and carried him out; at Daming Palace blood streamed from his nose across his face and he was killed at once — he was fourteen.

sentences.zh: 不脫靴，裹以席，埋於室內。

translations.literal: He was not stripped of his boots; wrapped in a mat he was buried indoors.
translations.idiomatic: His boots were never removed; wrapped in a mat, he was buried inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝使啟太后，臨哭十餘聲，便擁入殿。

translations.literal: The emperor had someone notify the empress dowager; she wailed a dozen times and was immediately ushered into the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent word to the empress dowager; she wailed only a dozen cries before they hustled her into the hall.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，葬於鄴西，贈謚曰楚恭哀帝，以慰太后。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year he was buried west of Ye; posthumously honored as Emperor Gong'ai of Chu, to console the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The following third month he was buried west of Ye; posthumously he was titled Emperor Gong'ai of Chu, to comfort the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 有遺腹四男，生數月皆幽死。

translations.literal: There were four posthumous sons; after a few months all were secretly killed.
translations.idiomatic: Four posthumous sons were born; within months all were secretly killed.

sentences.zh: 以平陽王淹孫世俊嗣。

translations.literal: Prince Yan of Pingyang's grandson Shijun was made heir.
translations.idiomatic: Shijun, grandson of Prince Yan of Pingyang, was made heir.

sentences.zh: 儼妃，李祖欽女也，進為楚帝后，居宣則宮。

translations.literal: Yan's consort was the daughter of Li Zuqin; she was advanced to empress of the Emperor of Chu and resided in Xuanze Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's consort was Li Zuqin's daughter; she was raised to empress of the Emperor of Chu and lived in Xuanze Palace.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，乃嫁焉。

translations.literal: When Qi fell she remarried.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell she remarried.

sentences.zh: 齊安王廓，字仁弘，武成第四子也。

translations.literal: Prince Kuo of Qi'an, courtesy name Renhong, was Wucheng's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kuo of Qi'an, courtesy name Renhong, was Gao Zhan's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 性長者，無過行。

translations.literal: By nature a worthy elder, he had no misdeeds.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was a man of worth; he had no misdeeds.

sentences.zh: 位特進、開府、儀同三司、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He held the rank of special advance, opening-establishment grand master, honorary-equal thirds grand master, and governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He held special advance, opening-establishment, honorary-equal thirds grand master, and the governorship of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 北平王貞，字仁堅，武成第五子也。

translations.literal: Prince Zhen of Beiping, styled Renjian, was the fifth son of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhen of Beiping, styled Renjian, was the fifth son of Gao Zhan.

sentences.zh: 沈審寬恕。

translations.literal: Deeply thoughtful and magnanimous in pardon.
translations.idiomatic: He was composed in judgment and generous in forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 帝常曰：「此兒得我鳳毛。

translations.literal: The emperor often said: "This boy has my phoenix down.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often said, "This boy has inherited my finest plumage.

sentences.zh: 」位司州牧、京畿大都督，兼尚書令、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: " He held in succession the ranks of Governor of Si Province, Grand Commander of the Capital Region, and concurrently Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: " He held in succession the governorship of Si Province, grand command of the capital region, and the concurrent posts of chief minister and recorder of affairs of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 帝行幸，總留臺事。

translations.literal: When the emperor went on tour, he was left in overall charge of affairs at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled, he was left in overall charge of the capital.

sentences.zh: 積年，後主以貞長大，漸忌之。

translations.literal: Over the years, as Zhen grew to maturity, the Later Lord came gradually to be wary of him.
translations.idiomatic: Over the years, as Zhen came of age, the Later Lord grew wary of him.

sentences.zh: 阿那肱承旨，令馮士幹劾繫貞於獄，奪其留後權。

translations.literal: Anaogong, reading the emperor's intent, had Feng Shigan impeach and imprison Zhen, stripping him of his authority as regent in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Anaogong, reading the emperor's intent, had Feng Shigan impeach Zhen and imprison him, stripping him of his authority as regent in the capital.

sentences.zh: 高平王仁英，武成第六子也。

translations.literal: Prince Renying of Gaoping was the sixth son of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Renying of Gaoping was the sixth son of Gao Zhan.

sentences.zh: 舉止軒昂，精神無檢格。

translations.literal: His bearing was lofty and dignified; his spirit was unfettered by restraint.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was lofty and dignified, his spirit unbound by constraint.

sentences.zh: 位定州刺史。

translations.literal: He held the post of Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 淮南王仁光，武成第七子也。

translations.literal: Prince Renguang of Huainan was the seventh son of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Renguang of Huainan was the seventh son of Gao Zhan.

sentences.zh: 性躁且暴，位清都尹。

translations.literal: He was by nature impulsive and violent; he held the post of Magistrate of Qingdu.
translations.idiomatic: He was impulsive and violent by nature and served as Magistrate of Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 次西河王仁幾，生而無骨，不自支持；

translations.literal: Next came Prince Renji of Xihe, who from birth lacked firm bone and could not support himself;
translations.idiomatic: Next came Prince Renji of Xihe, born without firm bone, unable to support himself;

sentences.zh: 次樂平王仁邕；

translations.literal: next, Prince Renyong of Leping;
translations.idiomatic: next, Prince Renyong of Leping;

sentences.zh: 次潁川王仁儉；

translations.literal: next, Prince Renjian of Yingchuan;
translations.idiomatic: next, Prince Renjian of Yingchuan;

sentences.zh: 次安樂王仁雅，從小有喑疾；

translations.literal: next, Prince Renya of Anle, who had been mute from childhood;
translations.idiomatic: next, Prince Renya of Anle, mute from childhood;

sentences.zh: 次丹陽王仁直；

translations.literal: next, Prince Renzhi of Danyang;
translations.idiomatic: next, Prince Renzhi of Danyang;

sentences.zh: 次東海王仁謙。

translations.literal: and last, Prince Renqian of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: and last, Prince Renqian of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 皆養於北宮。

translations.literal: All were raised in the Northern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: All were raised in the Northern Palace.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王死後，諸王守禁彌切。

translations.literal: After the Prince of Langya died, the restrictions on the princes grew ever stricter.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Langya died, the princes were kept under ever tighter guard.

sentences.zh: 武平末年，仁邕已下始得出外，供給儉薄，取充而已。

translations.literal: In the closing years of Wuping, Renyong and those below him were at last allowed to go outside; their provisions were miserly, barely enough to subsist.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of Wuping, Renyong and those below him were at last allowed outside; their provisions were meager, barely enough to live on.

sentences.zh: 尋後主窮蹙，以廓為光州，貞為青州，仁英為冀州，仁儉為膠州，仁直為濟州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long, with the Later Lord hard pressed, Kuo was assigned Guang Province, Zhen Qing Province, Renying Ji Province, Renjian Jiao Province, and Renzhi was made Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, with the Later Lord hard pressed, Kuo was sent to Guang Province, Zhen to Qing Province, Renying to Ji Province, Renjian to Jiao Province, and Renzhi was made Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 自廓已下，多與後主死於長安。

translations.literal: From Kuo downward, most died at Chang'an together with the Later Lord.
translations.idiomatic: From Kuo downward, most died at Chang'an with the Later Lord.

sentences.zh: 仁英以清狂，仁雅以喑疾，獲免，俱徙蜀。

translations.literal: Renying was spared on account of his pure madness; Renya on account of his muteness; both were exiled to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Renying was spared for his innocent eccentricity, Renya for his muteness; both were exiled to Shu.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，追仁英，詔與蕭琮、陳叔寶修其本宗祭禮。

translations.literal: During the Kaihuang era of Sui, Renying was summoned back; an edict ordered him, together with Xiao Cong and Chen Shubao, to restore the sacrificial rites of their ancestral houses.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era of Sui, Renying was recalled; an edict ordered him, with Xiao Cong and Chen Shubao, to restore the sacrificial rites of their ancestral houses.

sentences.zh: 未幾而卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 後主五男：穆皇后生幼主，諸姬生東平王恪，次善德，次買德，次質錢。

translations.literal: The Later Lord had five sons: Empress Mu bore the Young Lord; various consorts bore Prince Ke of Dongping, then Shande, then Maide, then Zhiqian.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord had five sons: Empress Mu bore the Young Lord; various consorts bore Prince Ke of Dongping, then Shande, then Maide, then Zhiqian.

sentences.zh: 胡太后以恪嗣琅邪王，尋夭折。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Hu had Ke succeed to the line of the Prince of Langya; he soon died young.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu had Ke succeed to the Prince of Langya's line; he soon died young.

sentences.zh: 齊滅，周武帝以任城已下大小三十王歸長安，皆有封爵。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou brought to Chang'an some thirty princes great and small from the Prince of Rencheng downward, all granting them ranks and fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou brought to Chang'an some thirty princes great and small from the Prince of Rencheng downward, all granting them ranks and fiefs.

sentences.zh: 其後不從戮者散配西土，皆死邊。

translations.literal: Afterward those who had not been executed were scattered to the western frontier, all dying on the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward those spared execution were scattered to the western frontier, all dying on the borders.

sentences.zh: 論曰：文襄諸子，咸有風骨，雖文雅之道，有謝間平，然武藝英姿，多堪禦侮。

translations.literal: Discussion: The sons of Wenxiang all possessed striking presence; though in the way of cultured elegance they fell short of the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao, yet in martial skill and heroic bearing many were fit to repel insult.
translations.idiomatic: Discussion: Gao Cheng's sons all had striking presence; though in cultured elegance they fell short of the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao, in martial skill and heroic bearing many were fit to repel insult.

sentences.zh: 縱咸陽賜劍，覆敗有徵，若使蘭陵獲全，未可量也，而終見誅翦，以至土崩，可為太息者矣。

translations.literal: Even if swords were granted at Xianyang, signs of overturn were already there; had the Prince of Lanling been preserved whole, what might have been cannot be measured — and yet in the end they were cut down one after another, until the state collapsed in ruin. A matter for deepest sighing indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Even if swords were granted at Xianyang, signs of ruin were already plain; had the Prince of Lanling been preserved whole, what might have been cannot be measured — yet in the end they were cut down one after another until the state collapsed. A matter for deepest sighing.

sentences.zh: 安德以時艱主暗，匿跡韜光，及平陽之陣，奮其忠勇，蓋以臨難見危，義深家國。

translations.literal: Ande, finding the times perilous and the ruler benighted, hid his tracks and kept his light under a bushel; yet at the battle of Pingyang he summoned his loyal valor — for facing peril in crisis, his devotion to house and state ran deep.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong of Ande, finding the times perilous and the ruler benighted, hid his tracks and kept his light under a bushel; yet at the battle of Pingyang he summoned his loyal valor — for facing peril in crisis, his devotion to house and state ran deep.

sentences.zh: 德昌大舉，事迫羣情，理至淪亡，無所歸命。

translations.literal: When Dezhi launched his great action, affairs pressed the feelings of the multitude; the logic led to extinction, with nowhere left to turn for deliverance.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezhi launched his great action, affairs pressed the feelings of the multitude; the logic led to extinction, with nowhere left to turn for deliverance.

sentences.zh: 廣寧請出後宮，竟不獲遂，非孝珩辭致有謝李同，自是後主心識去平原已遠。

translations.literal: Guangning's request to leave the inner palace was never fulfilled — not that Xiaoxheng's words lacked the persuasiveness of Li Tong; from that time the Later Lord's heart and mind had already drifted far from Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guangning's request to leave the inner palace was never granted — not that Xiaoxheng's words lacked the persuasiveness of Li Tong; from that time the Later Lord's heart and mind had already drifted far from Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 存亡事異，安可同年而說。

translations.literal: The matters of survival and destruction differ — how can they be spoken of in the same breath?
translations.idiomatic: Survival and destruction are not the same matter — how can they be spoken of in one breath?

sentences.zh: 武成殘忍姦穢，事極人倫。

translations.literal: Wucheng was cruel, licentious, and corrupt — his conduct pushed the bounds of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhan was cruel, licentious, and corrupt — his conduct pushed the bounds of human relations.

sentences.zh: 太原跡異猜嫌，情非釁逆，禍起昭信，遂及淫刑。

translations.literal: Taiyuan's conduct seemed strange and bred suspicion; in sentiment there was no rebellion, yet disaster arose from Zhaoxin, and thus came excessive punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Shaode of Taiyuan's conduct seemed strange and bred suspicion; in sentiment there was no rebellion, yet disaster arose from Empress Zhaoxin, and thus came excessive punishments.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 欲求長世，未之有也。

translations.literal: To seek long endurance — never yet has such a thing been seen.
translations.idiomatic: To seek long endurance — never yet has such a thing been seen.

sentences.zh: 以孝昭德音，庶可慶流後嗣，百年之酷，蓋濟南之濫觴。

translations.literal: One might have hoped that Xiaozhao's virtuous reputation could bring blessing down upon later generations, but a century of cruelty — perhaps Jinan was the headwater whence it all flowed.
translations.idiomatic: One might have hoped that Xiaozhao's virtuous reputation could bring blessing down upon later generations, but a century of cruelty — perhaps Jinan was the headwater whence it all flowed.

sentences.zh: 其云「莫效前人」之言，可為傷嘆，各愛其子，豈其然乎？

translations.literal: His words, 'Do not imitate your predecessors' — how they stir one's grief! That each man loves his own son — can it really be so?
translations.idiomatic: His words, "Do not imitate your predecessors" — how they stir one's grief! That each man loves his own son — can it really be so?

sentences.zh: 琅邪雖無師傅之資，而早聞氣尚。

translations.literal: The Prince of Langya, though without tutors' instruction, had early shown noble character.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Langya, though without tutors' instruction, had early shown noble character.

sentences.zh: 士開淫亂，多歷歲年，一朝勦絕，慶集朝野，以之受斃，深可痛焉。

translations.literal: He Shikai's licentious misrule had endured for many years; in a single morning it was cut down, and joy filled court and countryside — that for this he should meet his death is deeply painful.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai's licentious misrule had endured for many years; in a single morning it was cut down, and joy filled court and countryside — that for this he should meet his death is deeply painful.

sentences.zh: 然專戮之釁，未之或免，贈帝謚恭，矯枉過直，觀過知仁，不亦異於是乎？

translations.literal: Yet the offense of unauthorized killing could not be entirely set aside; to posthumously grant him the imperial title and the epithet Gong — to straighten the crooked went too far. To discern benevolence through one's faults — is this not different from that principle?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the offense of unauthorized killing could not be entirely set aside; to posthumously grant him the imperial title and the epithet Gong — to straighten the crooked went too far. To discern benevolence through one's faults — is this not different from that principle?

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
translations.idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
